## Deploy (probe-gw only; memento-agent untouched throughout)

$ ast spec validate -f astropods.yml
astropods.yml is valid
# agent.interfaces: {frontend: true, messaging: true} nested under agent:;
# container serves a static page + /health on $PORT (80 in production),
# no auth guard; Dockerfile stays root, EXPOSE 80; model unchanged.

$ ast push probe-gw --yes
probe-gw  tag <build-page>
$ ast agent redeploy --name probe-gw --latest --adapter web --wait
Running, Launch URL https://<chat-host>, build <build-page>

## Anonymous page check, pre-flip (no cookies, no auth)

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'code=%{http_code} redirect=%{redirect_url}' https://<chat-host>/
code=302 redirect=https://login.<host>/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<client-id>&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2F<chat-host>%2Foauth2%2Fidpresponse&response_type=code&scope=openid%20email&state=<sso-state>
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'code=%{http_code} redirect=%{redirect_url}' https://<chat-host>/health
code=302 redirect=https://login.<host>/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<client-id>&...&state=<sso-state>
# 302 to the platform SSO on both paths: sign-in still enforced at the
# front door. No-login serving is NOT possible in this state.

## Model turn through the messaging proxy (CLI login in memory, browser UA)

send -> 200 {"message_id": "<id>", "timestamp": "<timestamp>"}
history -> 200 2 messages (user turn present, no assistant text, as before)

## Access state (read-only)

$ ast agent access get --name probe-gw
web     user=<user-id>            (one owner)
slack   members of the agent's account (no grants set)
custom  members of the agent's account (no grants set)
# CLI offers `anyone` (= any signed-in user) but no public option.

## Billing

before deploy:  usage $0.29, credit left $9.71
after deploy:   usage $0.30, credit left $9.70
after turn 1:   trace $0.0056
after turn 2:   trace $0.0057, usage $0.35, credit left $9.65
# Post-flip verification (user switched Public ON in the console)

$ ast billing get
usage $0.60 (up from $0.35; the delta is concurrent tasks' spend, not
this check — anonymous GETs and billing reads cost nothing)

$ ast agent get --name probe-gw --json   # read-only: TWO external URLs
messaging: https://<chat-host>      (built-in chat; always signed in)
frontend:  https://<frontend-host>   (dedicated container hostname; NEW —
           the earlier probes hit the chat host, not the page)

$ curl anonymous https://<frontend-host>/ https://<frontend-host>/health
code=302 redirect=https://login.<host>/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<client-id>&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2F<frontend-host>%2Foauth2%2Fidpresponse&... (both paths)
$ sleep 180; curl again -> still 302 to the SSO login on both paths.

$ ast agent access get --name probe-gw   # read-only, unchanged
web     user=<user-id>
slack   members of the agent's account (no grants set)
custom  members of the agent's account (no grants set)
# CLI shows no Public flag; the toggle is console-only and not reflected here.

Outcome: the flip did NOT take effect on anonymous traffic. No-login
serving is NOT proven. Nothing was changed on the deployment (no push,
no redeploy, no access set) — verification was GETs only.

## Second post-flip check (flip confirmed on probe-gw this time)

The earlier flip had landed on `memento-agent` by mistake; the user
confirmed `probe-gw` itself is now Public (custom-app/frontend access, on
the deployment). Anonymous `GET /` and `/health` on the frontend host:
still **302 to the platform SSO login**, immediately and after a
3-minute wait; `access get` unchanged (CLI surfaces no Public flag).
Billing $0.60 → $0.64 from concurrent tasks; this check cost nothing.
Nothing changed (GETs + read-only CLI only). Verdict: **STILL-BLOCKED** —
the console Public toggle does not remove the front-door sign-in on the
frontend hostname. The no-login question now needs the platform: file the
gap (Public documented only in the adapter-auth warning, never observed
working) as an Astropods issue with this evidence, and keep the
public-shopper-page task unscheduled until anonymous 200 is observed.
